title: Empirical Evaluation of a Deterministic-Validator Guard for LLM→NetOps Generate→Verify→Repair Pipelines (Revised)
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory experiment that measures the operational impact of inserting a deterministic network-configuration validator into an LLM-driven generate→verify→repair (GVR) loop for intent→configuration NetOps tasks. Using a reproducible synthetic 200-task multi-vendor intent bank and a single hosted model (gpt-5-mini) under an adapter contract (≤1 automated repair call per task), each task produced one shared initial candidate; the guarded artifact was the final configuration after deterministic validation and, if invoked, a single automated repair. Primary estimand: paired absolute difference in actionable-misconfiguration rate (guarded − baseline), implemented as paired success-rate difference per the preregistration. Results (N=200 pairs): baseline valid-config count = 199/200 (0.995), guarded valid-config count = 200/200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005 (0.5 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided test p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). The preregistered primary hypothesis (≥50% relative reduction in actionable misconfigurations under original power assumptions) is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence (1/200) was far lower than assumed in the preregistered power calculation. We reconcile estimand algebra, provide detailed execution accounting, and publish cryptographic digests and authoritative artifact pointers for forensic verification.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) promise to streamline NetOps by translating operator intent into device-specific configuration changes at scale. However, incorrect generated commands can cause outages or violate workflow/policy constraints. For production proposals, practitioners often interpose deterministic validators and limited automated repair loops as guardrails in generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines. Despite this common engineering pattern, rigorously preregistered quantification of the marginal operational benefit of a deterministic validator under a bounded adapter contract (single hosted model, limited repairs) is uncommon and rarely accompanied by cryptographic artifact traceability.

We preregistered and executed study cnsmspec2026_gvr_v1_prereg_001 (SHA-256 = 5cb8a30815eacf0a3ca659d1a54fbaa71218e5ce57c0b13e2658099eb7da6ee4) to answer: How much does integrating a deterministic network validator into an LLM-driven GVR pipeline reduce actionable misconfiguration rates (paired comparison) on a 200-task synthetic multi-vendor NetOps task bank, and what residual error types persist after automated repairs? Our primary contribution is a fully preregistered, artifact-hashed paired confirmatory run with deterministic validator traces, explicit provider-call accounting, and complete analysis artifacts that enable forensic recomputation of the contingency table and per-episode traces.
sections.related_work: Deterministic pre-deployment network verification techniques (header-space analysis, incremental checkers, VeriFlow) are well established for checking forwarding correctness and policy properties. Recent LLM→NetOps work evaluates intent-driven configuration generation and presents accuracy-style leaderboards (NetConfEval and others), but typically without preregistration or end-to-end deterministic validator traces. Prior generate–validate–repair architectures have been proposed in software engineering (program repair) and AIOps, yet few studies publish cryptographic digests for provider calls and per-episode deterministic validator outputs. Our study differs by (1) holding the initial LLM candidate constant across conditions (shared_initial generation), (2) using a deterministic validator that emits canonical ASTs and simulator-backed semantic checks, (3) bounding automated repair attempts to at most one per task (adapter-enforced), and (4) publishing authoritative artifact hashes so auditors can reconstruct all reported counts.
sections.methodology:
Design and preregistration. The study used a preregistered paired-binary design with N=200 intent→configuration tasks sampled from a deterministic synthetic multi-vendor task bank. The preregistered primary_estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline (success = not actionable-error). The confirmatory test specified in the preregistration is an exact McNemar two-sided test; we additionally prespecified a paired-bootstrap (percentile) 95% CI with 10,000 resamples (seed 1729). The preregistration documents sampling, stratification plan (planned strata: Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67), adapter contract, retry/missingness rules, multiplicity plan, and analysis producer verifiers (all archived; preregistration SHA-256 above).

Adapter and model contract. Execution used adapter_family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1 and declared_model_version = gpt-5-mini (execution/model_configuration.json SHA-256 = a40e96e212ab87da251ac0d6dbb75bc543afa13438b5a6b9ebd073597ffdd820). The adapter enforced shared_initial generation semantics (a single initial candidate per task reused across baseline and guarded conditions) and a maximum of one automated repair call per task. Provider-call accounting is recorded in analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...) and execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...). Execution used model_calls_used = 201 (200 shared_initial + 1 repair) per the execution manifest (execution/execution_manifest.json hash available in the archive).

Synthetic tasks, validator, and scoring. Tasks were generated by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5; each task includes initial_state, expected_final_state, allowed touched fields, and explicit workflow policies (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields). The deterministic validator deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator id and version recorded in per-episode JSONs) performs (a) vendor-aware parsing into canonical ASTs, (b) syntactic and vendor parse checks, (c) intent-constraint enforcement (required_sequence, protected interfaces), and (d) simulator-backed semantic checks producing a binary score using scoring_rule = full_intent_constraint_validation. The validator emits validator_trace objects (validation_before, validation_after) that record parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and final_state—these per-episode JSONs are authoritative and archived under execution/scoring/ (representative examples and hashes in the evidence bundle).

Execution, retries, and missingness handling. The preregistered retry policy allowed up to two automatic retries on provider-call failures; unresolved call failures would lead to task exclusion per the missingness plan. No provider-call failures occurred. Execution manifest: planned_episode_count = 400 (200 pairs × 2 conditions), completed_episode_count = 400, failed_episode_count = 0, complete_pair_count = 200. analysis/missingness_summary.csv (SHA-256 = 808b3c00...) records zero missing or excluded episodes. All provider calls, retries (none), and stage counts are logged and hashed for reproducibility.

Statistical analysis. The paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor consumed the raw results (execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) and produced the 2×2 contingency table (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051ba...), an exact McNemar two-sided p-value, and a paired-bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). We preserved the preregistered multiplicity plan (one primary confirmatory hypothesis) and labeled all other tests exploratory. Analysis logs and CSVs are archived and hashed (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).
sections.results:
Primary paired outcome (artifact-grounded). Complete_pair_count = 200; baseline_success_count = 199 (0.995); guarded_success_count = 200 (1.000); absolute paired change (guarded − baseline) = 0.005. Contingency-cell counts (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA-256 = 658051bae1f10d90aed1728b8d20dd3700a5694b68b02f1b0c118c45d9414db0): n_11 = 199 (guarded=1 & baseline=1), n_10 = 1 (guarded=1 & baseline=0; guarded-only improvement), n_01 = 0 (guarded=0 & baseline=1), n_00 = 0 (both invalid). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI for the absolute paired difference = [0.0, 0.015] (10,000 resamples, seed 1729). All analysis artifacts are archived with SHA-256 digests listed in the Disclosure Statement.

Estimand algebra and hypothesis reconciliation. The preregistered primary_estimand is an absolute paired difference in success rates; the preregistration textual hypothesis described a relative reduction in actionable-error rate (≥50%). For clarity we present the algebraic mapping using observed data: baseline_error_rate = 1 − baseline_success_rate = 1 − 0.995 = 0.005 (1/200). guarded_error_rate = 1 − guarded_success_rate = 0.0. The observed relative reduction in actionable-error rate = (baseline_error_rate − guarded_error_rate) / baseline_error_rate = (0.005 − 0)/0.005 = 1.0 (100% relative reduction). However, the preregistered power calculation targeted detection of an absolute reduction ≈0.15 (15 percentage points) with N=200; because the observed baseline error prevalence (0.005) is far smaller than assumed at design time, the confirmatory test (sized for large absolute effects) lacks sensitivity to draw the preregistered claim despite the observed relative reduction. Thus the preregistered confirmatory conclusion is that H1 is not supported under the original power/decision rule; we document this reconciliation transparently and point auditors to the archived contingency CSV and analysis logs for exactness.

Representative artifact diagnostics. The single discordant improvement (n_10 = 1) is a per-episode record in the raw results and per-episode scoring JSONs archived under execution/raw_results.jsonl and execution/scoring/ (SHA-256s in Disclosure). Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 201 and stage_counts = {shared_initial_generation: 200, repair: 1} per analysis/deterministic_reconciliation.json (SHA-256 = 8a2b85f8...). Missingness and contamination summaries show no model-call failures or systematic contamination (analysis/contamination_summary.csv SHA-256 = 389227f0...).
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation. Under the constrained test regime (synthetic 200-task bank, single model gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator v5, and single automated repair), the guarded pipeline produced a numerically small absolute improvement because the baseline generator produced extremely few actionable errors (1/200). In practice the operational benefit of deterministic validators depends on baseline LLM error prevalence, validator semantic coverage, repair budget, human-in-the-loop cost, and risk tolerance. Our results show that in a low-baseline-error regime the marginal reduction in actionable misconfigurations may be tiny in absolute terms even if relative reductions appear large; designers should therefore align validation investment with expected baseline error rates and cost-of-failure.

Design and power lessons. The preregistered power calculation assumed a much higher baseline actionable-error prevalence (targeting detectability of an absolute reduction ≈0.15). Observing baseline_error_rate = 0.005 demonstrates that (1) planned effect-size assumptions should match empirically plausible baseline failure rates and (2) for rare-event regimes researchers should either enlarge N, oversample high-difficulty tasks, or use cost-weighted estimands to power confirmatory inferences. We include a compact artifact-grounded sensitivity note: with observed baseline_error_rate = 0.005 and N=200, the absolute differences detectable at conventional power are orders of magnitude larger than the observed 0.005; analysis logs show this mismatch and are archived (analysis/analysis_log.jsonl SHA-256 = dbc0bd6b...).

Reviewer-requested items and archival practice. Reviewers requested (i) per-vendor stratified observed counts and (ii) explicit discordant episode identifier(s). The preregistered planned stratum totals (Cisco-like N=66; Juniper-like N=67; RFC-neutral N=67) were executed without exclusions; therefore observed per-stratum totals equal those planned counts. Per-stratum success/failure breakdowns and the explicit discordant episode identifier are deterministically retrievable from execution/task_manifest.jsonl (SHA-256 = 4b28215e8a611feda50f6284058083b9ffcc2f5881f557081ce9e9f890f1c78a) together with execution/raw_results.jsonl (SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c87db4742c807240b5ee18f934aaf45848350b3840f92af401bcb68d02) and the per-episode scoring JSONs under execution/scoring/ (full hash manifest in execution/execution_manifest.json). We provide authoritative artifact pointers and SHA-256 digests (Disclosure) to preserve forensic traceability rather than re-publish per-episode identifiers verbatim in the body where those strings are not otherwise printed in the supplied evidence bundle.

Threats to validity and limitations (summary). Internal validity threats include prompt sensitivity and the single-repair budget constrained by the adapter; construct validity is limited by the synthetic task bank and by the validator's semantic scope; external validity is constrained by single-model evidence (gpt-5-mini) and non-production task realism; conclusion validity is affected by rare-event statistics (baseline_error_rate = 0.005) leading to low discordant-pair mass and wide uncertainty for small absolute effects. We enumerate precise limitations in the dedicated section and archive all artifacts to enable external reanalysis.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment evaluating a deterministic-validator guard for an LLM→NetOps GVR pipeline under a bounded adapter contract. On the synthetic 200-task bank with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline reduced actionable misconfigurations from 1/200 to 0/200 (absolute paired change = 0.005). The preregistered large-effect hypothesis is not supported because the observed baseline error prevalence was substantially lower than assumed in power planning. We publish cryptographic hashes and precise artifact paths for all principal inputs, provider calls, validator traces, and analysis outputs so auditors can recompute contingency tables, per-vendor stratified counts, and the exact discordant episode identifier from the archived evidence. Future work should broaden model coverage, validator diversity, repair budgets, and task realism to identify regimes where validator-assisted repair produces materially large operational risk reductions.

limitations: Single-model evidence: only gpt-5-mini was used; results do not imply multi-model generality.
Synthetic task bank and validator scope: the 200-task benchmark and deterministic validator semantics bound external validity to production networks.
Low baseline error prevalence: baseline actionable-error rate = 1/200, limiting power to detect moderate relative improvements and making effect-size estimates imprecise for rare failure regimes.
Single automated repair attempt: the adapter contract permitted at most one automated repair per task; multi-attempt repair effects are unexplored.
Single deterministic validator implementation: validator coverage or implementation choices influence measured outcomes; different validators may yield different paired results.

Untestable preregistered secondary hypothesis (H2): because guarded residual failures = 0, the preregistered confirmatory contingency test comparing residual error-type proportions could not be executed and any error-type comments are exploratory.

Reviewer-requested per-vendor stratified observed counts and explicit discordant episode identifier are deterministically retrievable from archived artifacts (execution/task_manifest.jsonl SHA-256 = 4b28215e..., execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA-256 = 9eeaa0c8...) but are not printed verbatim in the supplied manuscript evidence bundle; auditors can compute them from the archived JSONs.
